TAGLINE: Mechanistic Subnetwork Pruning: Diagnosing and recovering from catastrophic layer sensitivity in transformers — scaling to Mistral-7B with true hardware compression.
OVERVIEW: A structured pruning + activation healing pipeline (TIM-MGDT) that identifies which transformer layers and MLP widths are elastic vs critical. By exploiting the 'Hardware-Aligned Structural Lottery Ticket' hypothesis, we prune models like Mistral-7B using FIM metrics while fully preserving zero-shot reasoning (GSM8K) capabilities.

Existing pruning methods either destroy quality or require expensive retraining. We discovered that width pruning based on empirical FIM preserves zero-shot logical reasoning significantly better than depth pruning (which suffers from the 'Perplexity Trap'). We align all pruned layers to Tensor Core dimensions (ceil/floor rounding) ensuring theoretical FLOP reductions map directly to physical wall-clock latency gains.

Phase 16 active. We are currently running a smart multi-GPU evaluation of the hardware-aware FIM width-pruned Mistral-7B. We are gathering definitive GSM8K evidence to prove our 'Hardware-Aligned Structural Lottery Ticket' hypothesis, demonstrating that width pruning avoids the catastrophic disruption seen in full layer dropping.
RESEARCH_Q: Can empirical FIM metrics reliably identify and exploit elasticity in MLP internal dimensions to achieve structured, hardware-aligned compression at 20%+ sparsity without destroying zero-shot reasoning (GSM8K)?

FIM Width Pruning over Depth Pruning

Depth pruning (layer dropping) creates sharp, localized discontinuities ('Perplexity Trap'). Width pruning (MLP dimensionality reduction) guided by Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) preserves the structural manifold and retains zero-shot logical reasoning better.
To ensure theoretical FLOP reductions translate to physical speedups, we round pruned MLP dimensions to nearest 64 (Tensor Core alignment) via specific ceil/floor strategies.
